insight.title: How the invisible dance shapes your morning
insight.subtitle: Beneath the surface of the stillest room, everything is in motion

sections.text: You are standing in a room that is never still. Even when the air feels silent and your coffee looks motionless, a frantic energy hums beneath. Every object holds a sea of vibrating particles, bumping together in an endless rush. We live inside a world that is constantly, quietly shivering.

This secret movement is what we call heat. When you hold a warm mug, you feel a literal transfer of motion. Fast-moving molecules in the clay strike the slower ones in your palms, sharing momentum like tiny billiard balls. It is an invisible negotiation between every object you touch.

This hidden system ensures that nothing remains isolated. Every breath you take and every step you make adjusts the temperature of the universe. We are not just observers, but participants in a grand balance. Your smallest gesture ripples outward, changing the rhythm of the molecules around you forever.
Warmth is the feeling of the universe sharing its energy with you.

news.title: Trump holds press conference on Iran : NPR
news.description: The president has had mixed messages about how and when the U.S.-Israel-led war in Iran will end.
news.why: War escalation could lead to higher fuel and travel costs.

news.title: 'Assassinations won’t stop us': Mojtaba Khamenei defies Trump’s escalating threats
news.description: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei vowed that assassinations and strikes will not weaken its military, as US President Donald Trump warned of attacks on power plants and potential oil seizure.
news.why: Ongoing military tensions could disrupt global shipping and product availability.

news.title: Key Fed official sees possible rate hike amid higher gas prices, inflation concerns
news.description: A top Federal Reserve official said Monday that an interest rate hike could be appropriate if inflation remains persistently above the central bank’s 2% target, the latest sign that some policymakers are moving away from a bias toward reducing borrowing costs
news.why: Your monthly loan and mortgage payments could become more expensive.

news.title: March retail inflation seen at 3.5%: FE Poll, economists flag upside risks as energy prices firm up
news.description: Retail inflation likely rose to a 13-month high of 3.5% in March, driven by fuel price surge amid West Asia tensions, though still below RBI’s 4% target.
news.why: You may pay more for groceries and basic household goods soon.

news.title: China Eyes Space-Based Solar Power for Potential Military and Electronic Warfare Use
news.description: China's space solar power project, Sun Chase, could provide energy and serve as an electronic warfare tool, jamming signals or securing networks.
news.why: New satellite technologies might interfere with your mobile or GPS signals.

news.title: ‘A proud moment’: PM Modi hails India’s ‘defining step’ in civil nuclear journey as Kalpakkam fast breeder reactor attains criticality
news.description: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday said India had taken a “defining step” in its civil nuclear journey after the Prototype Fast Breeder.
news.why: New nuclear technology may eventually lead to cheaper and more reliable electricity.

news.title: Artemis II nears historic lunar flyby as Nasa tests path back to the Moon
news.description: Science News: BENGALURU: Four astronauts are now closing in on the Moon, as Nasa prepares for the most critical phase of its first crewed deep-space mission in over.
news.why: Space exploration breakthroughs will eventually improve global communication and weather tracking.
